overview: Custom Speed is a bhop-style movement modifier built on the fork's MovementEvent. On every tick the player is moving on the ground it forces motionY to 0.376 (scaled by the up multiplier to 0.387) and re-pins the horizontal speed to 1.61 blocks per tick; in the air the horizontal value decays by the friction setting (0.99) per tick down to the base move speed of 0.2873. The event setters are the wire: the fork's EntityPlayerSP.moveEntity override fires MovementEvent with the real motion deltas and applies the modified values, so the next C04 sent by func_175161_p carries the inflated speed.

sections.p: The fork overrides EntityPlayerSP.moveEntity to construct a MovementEvent from the incoming x, y and z, fire it on the event bus, and call super.moveEntity with the event's modified values. CustomSpeed writes event.setY (and the motionY field) and delegates the horizontal write to MovementUtils.setMoveSpeed, which projects the speed onto the movement input direction with the 45-degree diagonal blend. The modified motion then becomes the position delta of the next C03 or C04, so no packet is sent from the module itself; the fork's own movement send is the carrier.

isMovingOnGround (isMoving and onGround) triggers the re-pin: motionY becomes the MotionY setting and airSpeed becomes the Ground Speed setting. The vertical value is multiplied by the up multiplier when positive (1.03 default, giving 0.387) and by the down multiplier otherwise. In the air, airSpeed is multiplied by friction (0.99) each tick and clamped at the base move speed, so a hop starts at 1.61 and glides down to 0.2873 over roughly 170 ticks while the player holds a direction key.

1.61 blocks per tick is about 5.7 times the vanilla sprint rate of 0.2806 and far above the 0.2873 base the server's physics model expects after friction. The hop cadence is deterministic: one jump on every ground contact with no randomization of the vertical value, which removes the timing variance that separates a legit bhop from a script. The MotionY default of 0.376 sits below the vanilla 0.42 jump, so the vertical side is conservative; the horizontal pin is what every movement check sees.

files.label: CustomSpeed.java
files.explanation: The module file is the entire logic: a single MovementEvent handler with five settings. On a ground tick it re-pins motionY to the MotionY setting and airSpeed to the Ground Speed setting, applies the up or down multiplier to the vertical value, writes both the event y and the motionY field, decays airSpeed by friction, clamps it at the base move speed, and hands the horizontal write to MovementUtils.setMoveSpeed. The module holds airSpeed as instance state, so the decay curve survives across ticks and is re-armed on every ground contact.

files.label: MovementUtils.java (horizontal projection)
files.explanation: MovementUtils is where the module's horizontal write happens. setMoveSpeed(event, speed) reads the movement input, applies the same TargetStrafe steering the client's other movement modules use (it consults TargetStrafe.canStrafe and Aura.currentEntity when strafing), and writes the event x and z along the blended yaw. getBaseMoveSpeed returns the 0.2873 walk base scaled by the speed-potion amplifier, which is both the clamp floor for the module's friction decay and the value the anticheat-side models use as the legitimate expectation.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (horizontal speed envelope)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly is the NCP speed envelope; there is no separate NCP Speed check in this tree. The check() rebuilds the allowed horizontal distance via prepareSpeedEstimation, which predicts the next position from the 1.8 acceleration model (walk speed times 0.91 cubed over friction cubed, plus 30 percent for sprint), and compares it with the actual C04 delta. The module's first air move covers 1.61 blocks against a prediction around 0.31, so the offset is about 1.3 and the violation, computed as the sum of the horizontal and vertical excess times 100, lands near 130 on the first move and triggers the set-back.

The onGround true flag on every C04 does not help, because the check's ground state comes from a block-cache ray trace (RichBoundsLocation.isOnGround) rather than the packet flag, and the vertical side grants a jumpDelay window of 10 ticks for the 0.387 lift. The decay glide is also covered: any air tick above the predicted envelope accumulates, and the set-back keeps the player at the last accepted position, so the module cannot spend the friction curve at high speed.

countering.label: Speed (stage-based expectation)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Speed check models the horizontal expectation per phase. On the ground the expected value is the current move divided by ground time plus the 0.2873 base (ground time capped at 8 ticks); off the ground it stages by vertical speed, adding 0.049 for a level glide, 0.08 below 0.34, and 0.3261 above 0.34. The module's 1.61 exceeds even the rising-stage expectation of 0.6134, so every air tick flags under the BunnyHop label: the descending stage allows about 0.367 and the rising stage about 0.613, both far below the pin.

The jump-off on every ground contact keeps the ground-time allowance near one tick, which is the one branch that tolerates the magnitude, but the module spends almost all of its time in the air where both stages flag. The config defaults (block 0.6699, step modifier 0.489) are also below the pin, and the check stores the current position as the set-back on every pass, so the glide is interrupted on the first violation.

countering.label: Speed (momentum conservation)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Speed check conserves momentum: the expected speed is friction times the last speed plus the legal adders (the 0.2 sprint-jump boost when sprinting and jumping, water flow, and so on). With ground friction 0.6 the expected value after a hop lands around 0.33, and the module's pinned 1.61 produces a discrepancy of about 1.28 on the first move. The discrepancy accumulates per player and flags when the total crosses 0.1, adding discrepancy times 10 to the violation level and rubberbanding the player.

The 0.99 air friction does not help: the check compares against the physics model, not against the module's own decay curve, so every air tick contributes while the speed stays above the model. The no-move handling banks non-update moves as negative discrepancy, but the module's C04s are position updates, so that forgiveness does not apply.
